builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Depth Before Breadth: Reverse-to-Forward Curriculum with Advantage Decomposition for LLM Agent
summary: The technique replaces standard sparse-terminal-reward RL for LLM agents with paired advantage decomposition (separate signals for reaching solvable states and completing tasks) plus a reverse-to-forward curriculum along reference trajectories. It costs an RL training pipeline with repeated environment rollouts, reference trajectories, and additional advantage-estimation complexity, none of which fits inference-only or API-based workflows. It can fail when reference trajectories are unavailable or unrepresentative, when the environment cannot be sampled cheaply, or when the curriculum's capability-region assumption does not hold for the target task.
rationale: The method addresses sparse-reward credit assignment in agentic RL, but adopting it requires running RL fine-tuning with environment rollouts, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU budget for most production teams.
technique: Reverse-to-forward curriculum RL with paired advantage decomposition

claims.statement: The technique replaces standard sparse-terminal-reward RL for LLM agents with paired advantage decomposition (separate signals for reaching solvable states and completing tasks) plus a reverse-to-forward curriculum along reference trajectories. It costs an RL training pipeline with repeated environment rollouts, reference trajectories, and additional advantage-estimation complexity, none of which fits inference-only or API-based workflows. It can fail when reference trajectories are unavailable or unrepresentative, when the environment cannot be sampled cheaply, or when the curriculum's capability-region assumption does not hold for the target task.
Reports 90.1%/96.1% success on ALFWorld and 80.2%/82.6% on WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct, outperforming competitive agentic RL baselines at both scales; no multiplicative factor is stated.
